subject: Re: EdgeTech — Term mechanics: rolling renewal, notice carveouts, T4C scenarios
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@edgetech.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>; Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Ortega <rafael.ortega@edgetech.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial redline and a couple of termination questions

Hi Markus / Camila,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is our redline of the MSA + order form (EdgeTech_Redline_Sept20.docx) — the legal team flagged three items that are blocking approval on our side:

1) Term + auto-renew: EdgeTech prefers a 60-day notice to opt out of auto-renew, Redwood's standard is 90. We left both options in the bluelines; please confirm Redwood's flexibility.

2) Termination for convenience (T4C): Our procurement asks that T4C include a 30-day transition assistance window (data export + access to logs) and a pro-rated refund for pre-paid fees. Redwood's current T4C looks more limited.

3) Renewal alignment: For pilots that convert to paid, we want rolling renewal windows tied to the actual activation date (not invoice date) — this avoids forced billing cycles.

Can you confirm who on your side will pick up T4C language and whether you can accept a 60-day opt-out as a compromise? We need to get a final legal signoff by 09/27 to hit procurement timelines.

Attached: EdgeTech_Redline_Sept20.docx (track changes).

Best,
Maria Lopez
Sr. Counsel, EdgeTech Solutions
maria.lopez@edgetech.com
+1 415 555 0112

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@edgetech.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>; Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline and a couple of termination questions

Maria — thanks for the redline and the clear checklist. I reviewed with Camila and looped in Kimberly from Legal to take the lead on T4C specifics. Quick responses below and next steps:

- Auto-renew / notice window: We can be flexible on notice, but need to understand the downstream implications for Reserved/Dedicated capacity commitments. 60 days is something we can consider for standard hosted orders; if there is dedicated capacity in scope, we'll need a 90-day window or alternative ramp-down payment.

- T4C transition assistance: We are willing to commit to a 30-day data export and access to audit logs. We typically include a defined handback checklist (export formats, retention of logs for 30 days). Kimberly will propose language for the pro-rated refund mechanics.

- Rolling renewal: Agreed in principle. We'll propose a clause that ties the renewal anniversary to the activation date for the specific order form.

Camila: can you confirm whether the initial order includes any dedicated capacity? If yes, we should capture the 90 vs 60 carveout explicitly in the order form.

Kimberly: any legal constraints to propose updated T4C wording by EOD tomorrow (09/21)? If needed, we can schedule a 30-minute call with EdgeTech legal.

I'll attach a working Order Form draft that pulls in our standard fallback language for capacity items.

Attachments: RFQ_OrderForm_Draft_v2.docx

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
+1 650 555 2402

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@edgetech.com>; Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline and a couple of termination questions

Maria / team — I reviewed the EdgeTech redline and pulled the main T4C points into a short note (attached KP_T4C_Notes_20260921.pdf). Key proposals from Redwood Legal: 

- Notice window: propose a compromise of 60 days for hosted/shared capacity orders, 90 days for Dedicated/Reserved capacity. We'll add clear definitions for "Dedicated" in the Order Form to avoid ambiguity.

- Pro-rated refunds: Redwood will provide a pro-rated credit for unused pre-paid fees where cancellation occurs mid-term. We'll define the calculation in the Order Form schedule (days remaining / days in term * pre-paid amount), subject to any outstanding usage-based charges.

- Transition assistance: commit to 30 days of export + access to logs; Redwood will provide the export in commonly accepted formats (JSON/CSV) and a secure transfer method. We will not host historical export beyond 30 days without an addendum.

- Activation date renewal anchor: can do — we will add a paragraph: "Order Form term and renewal dates shall be measured from the date of activation of services for the specific Order."

I'm attaching a short redline and a proposed 1-paragraph T4C template. Markus — I left two places highlighted for Sales to confirm: (1) whether EdgeTech's purchase includes dedicated GPU pools; (2) whether they will require an escrow for customer data during the 30-day export window (uncommon, but they sometimes ask).

If EdgeTech accepts the split 60/90 approach, Legal can produce a consolidated redline by COB 09/22. If we need faster turnaround, please confirm and we'll schedule a 30-min call for 09/22 morning.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@edgetech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>; Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Ortega <rafael.ortega@edgetech.com>; Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline and a couple of termination questions

Kimberly / Markus — thanks for the detail and the split 60/90 approach, that addresses the capacity concern we raised. A few quick clarifications so we can proceed to signoff: 

1) Refund calculation: EdgeTech accepts the pro-rated refund formula you proposed, with the caveat that any unpaid usage charges billed after termination should be deducted.

2) Export: 30-day export window is acceptable. We do not require escrow for data; standard secure transfer is fine. Please confirm SFTP/HTTPS transfer option.

3) Rolling renewal anchor: confirmed — activation date is preferred.

We are comfortable with Legal producing a consolidated redline. Once we have that, Rafael (procurement) will do a last check and we can route to our CFO for approval. Our target is to receive the consolidated redline by COB 09/22 so procurement can sign on 09/24.

If you can push the consolidated redline, please include an explicit clause that for any Dedicated capacity order, Redwood will notify EdgeTech in writing 120 days ahead of any planned infrastructure decommissioning that could materially affect performance. That's a non-blocker but helps our platform team.

Attachments: none in this message.

Best,
Maria Lopez
Sr. Counsel, EdgeTech

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@edgetech.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>; Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-24T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline and a couple of termination questions

Thanks everyone — Kimberly will upload the consolidated redline to the shared drive and include the SFTP/HTTPS export language and the Dedicated-notice 120-day commitment for service-impact events. Camila and I will confirm order-level capacity type and call out any Dedicated line items in the Order Form before we publish.

Next steps: 
- Kimberly to upload consolidated redline by EOD 09/24 to https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-EdgeTech-Contract-Review and mark for EdgeTech review.
- Camila to confirm whether this initial purchase includes Dedicated capacity by 09/25 10:00 PT.
- Rafael / Maria to confirm procurement/CFO signoff targeted for 09/27 pending consolidated redline.

If all looks good we can prep DocuSign for signature on 09/28.

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.

Markus Klein
